findings.title: The derived website name bypasses the untrusted website restriction
findings.body: For anonymous viewers of TL0 users, `website` is intentionally omitted by `untrusted_attributes`, but `website_name` is a separate serialized attribute and is not subject to that restriction. The `include_website_name` method does not implement the serializer's `include_website_name?` predicate, so it does not prevent serialization. As a result, the website hostname and path can still be exposed to viewers who are meant not to see the website. Apply the same restriction to `website_name` and add a regression test with a populated website.

findings.title: Website labels drop explicit ports
findings.body: `URI#host` excludes the port, so a website such as `http://example.com:8443/user` is labeled `example.com/user` when the instance host matches, or just `example.com` otherwise. The link still targets port 8443, but the displayed label hides that part of its destination; the previous client-side parsing preserved it. Include the port in the serialized label when one is present.
